title: Concurrent manual triggers can queue duplicate podcast episodes for the same digest

evidence.quote:
episode = podcast_service.queue_episode_generation(
            session,
            digest_id=digest_id,
            user_id=user_id,
            force=False,
        )

all_episodes = session.exec(
            select(PodcastEpisode).order_by(PodcastEpisode.created_at.desc())
        ).all()
        episode = next(
            (ep for ep in all_episodes if digest_id_str in (ep.digest_ids or [])),
            None,
        )

episode = PodcastEpisode(
            digest_ids=[digest_id_str],
            trigger="manual",
            user_id=user_id,
            status="pending",
            created_at=now,
            updated_at=now,
        )
        session.add(episode)
        session.commit()
        session.refresh(episode)
        logger.info(
            "Podcast episode queued",
            extra={"digest_id": digest_id_str, "episode_id": str(episode.id), "force": force},
        )
        self._schedule_episode_task(episode.id)

reasoning: The POST route delegates every request directly to queue_episode_generation. That helper performs an application-level scan for an existing episode and, if none is found, inserts and schedules a new episode without a transaction-level lock or database uniqueness guard for the digest. Two simultaneous POST /digests/{digest_id}/podcast requests can both observe no existing episode, then both commit and schedule separate generation tasks, duplicating work and potentially TTS/LLM costs for the same digest.
reproduction: For a completed digest with no podcast episode, issue two concurrent authenticated POST requests to /api/digests/{digest_id}/podcast. If both requests reach the existence scan before either commit is visible, both can return 200 with different episode_id values and both tasks are scheduled.
recommendation: Make queueing atomic per digest. For SQLite, use a transaction/lock strategy such as BEGIN IMMEDIATE around the existence check and insert, or introduce a normalized digest-to-episode table with a unique digest_id constraint for manual single-digest episodes and handle the integrity conflict by returning the existing episode. Keep the route behavior idempotent under concurrent calls.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing route tests exercise a single sequential POST and a sequential failed-episode requeue path, but they do not send concurrent requests or assert that only one episode/task is created under contention.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that starts two concurrent POST /api/digests/{digest_id}/podcast calls for the same completed digest while delaying the service between the existence check and insert; assert that both responses reference the same episode or that the database contains exactly one episode for that digest and only one task is scheduled.
minimumFixScope: Update app/services/podcast_service.py to enforce atomic per-digest queueing, and add a focused concurrency regression test for the POST route or service.
